messages:
mia_customer: Hey team — we started seeing recurring 429s from our EdgeWriter fleet about ~03:40 UTC. It’s a very regular pulse every minute, lasts ~10s, then clears. All failures return 429 + Retry-After. Not sure if this is client-side backoff or an upstream RPM cap. Request IDs: req_abc123, req_def456.

sarah_support: Sorry for the hit — can you paste one full failing response (headers + small body) and confirm which API key/org? Also roughly how many pods/workers are making calls concurrently?

mia_customer: Headers from one failing response: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 600`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 12`, `Retry-After: 10`
logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-14T03:40:12Z edgewriter-5c7b Flush started
2026-03-14T03:40:12Z edgewriter-5c7b POST /v1/edges 50 items -> 429 (req_abc123)
2026-03-14T03:40:13Z edgewriter-1a2f POST /v1/edges 48 items -> 429 (req_def456)
```
We have 12 pods, each flushes their local buffer every 60s (default).

skeven_support: (typo) sorry — kevin here. That pattern screams synchronized flushes creating a per-minute "pulse" that exceeds the RPM. If your org limit is 600 RPM, and 12 pods each send ~50 requests near-identical time, you get ~600 bursts right at the boundary.

kevin_sre: Quick checklist: 1) confirm you’re using a single API key (shared across pods) — that aggregates to one RPM bucket; 2) look for cron-like alignment or clock-synchronized flush; 3) check X-RateLimit-* across responses; 4) capture a few request_ids and timestamps for us to correlate.

mia_customer: yes single key. flush is a cron triggered by system clock. we didn’t jitter.

devon_eng: Cause found. Two mitigation paths: immediate client-side smoothing + short-term quota bump while you roll out the smoothing. For smoothing: add randomized jitter on flush, limit concurrency per pod, and use exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s. Example pseudo: `delay = random(0, 60000/num_pods)` before flush.

sarah_support: I started a ticket to request a temporary quota increase. Ticket: S-98321. ratebot will post updates. If you want a Dedicated trial to avoid RPM caps longer-term we can propose that too.

ratebot: Ticket created: S-98321. Priority: P2. Assigned to infra-ops. ETA for initial review: 2 business days.

kevin_sre: Practical quick changes we recommend now (can be hotfixed client-side):
- per-pod concurrency cap: `CONCURRENCY=4`
- jitter before flush: `sleep(rand(0, 60000 / $POD_COUNT) / 1000)`
- backoff on 429: `sleep(min(60, base * 2^attempt) * random())`
- switch to bulk/batched endpoint if available to reduce # of requests

mia_customer: Would switching to streaming help? We have many small items, maybe stream them instead of individual posts.

devon_eng: Streaming or a batch endpoint will definitely reduce RPM. If you can batch 100 items per request instead of 1, you cut RPM by ~100x for the same throughput. Also persistent connections reduce connection overhead and allow pipelining.

sarah_support: Next steps from our side: we’ll correlate request_ids you provided (req_abc123, req_def456) against infra logs for the timeframe 2026-03-14 03:40–03:55 UTC. We’ll also leave the temporary quota ticket open until you confirm smoothing is in place.

kevin_sre: Quick reproducible test you can run locally to validate smoothing: run 12 clients that each send 50 requests to the API with no jitter -> you should see 429s. Repeat with jitter and capped concurrency -> 429s should disappear. If you want, post a small repro script and we can run it in our sandbox.

mia_customer: testing now. Implemented jitter + concurrency cap across pods. Also added exp backoff on 429s.

mia_customer: Update: after deploying jitter + concurrency cap we dropped from ~45 429s/min to ~2 429s/min in the same window. Looks much better.

sarah_support: Amazing, thanks for the quick turnaround :tada:. We’ll mark ticket S-98321 as pending verification. If you want us to temporarily increase RPM while you fully migrate to batching/streaming, reply here and we’ll expedite.

mia_customer: Not needed now, but keep the ticket open for 24h while we monitor. Will report back. Thanks all! :pray:
